media_work.title: The Central Park Five
media_work.creator_name: Ken Burns, Sarah Burns, David McMahon
media_work.focus_or_theme: Wrongful conviction, coerced false confessions, juvenile suspects, racial bias, media frenzy, DNA exoneration.
media_work.summaryNotes: Landmark case exposing issues with juvenile interrogations and false confessions.

media_item.focus_or_theme: Wrongful conviction, coerced false confessions, juvenile suspects, racial bias, media frenzy, DNA exoneration.
media_item.summary_notes: Provides a detailed account of the wrongful conviction of five teenagers in the high-profile "Central Park Jogger" case. It highlights the intense pressure, coercive interrogation tactics, and racial undertones that led to false confessions and convictions despite a lack of physical evidence connecting them. Their exoneration came years later when the actual perpetrator confessed and DNA confirmed his guilt. The case became a symbol of systemic flaws in the justice system, particularly regarding treatment of minority youth and reliance on confessions.

research_notes_other.notes_from_film_list.txt: Directed by Ken Burns, Sarah Burns, David McMahon; Examines the 1989 case of five Black and Latino teenagers wrongfully convicted. Available via PBS, Amazon, DVD.

featured_individuals.crime_convicted_of_raw: Assault, Rape, Robbery (related to attack on Trisha Meili)
featured_individuals.narrative_summary: Wrongfully convicted in 1990 for the 1989 attack on Trisha Meili, and exonerated in 2002 after serving between 6 and 13 years. His conviction was based on a coerced false confession obtained after lengthy interrogations without adequate counsel or parental presence. Received a settlement from NYC.
contributing_factors_raw: Coerced false confessions (obtained after lengthy interrogations without adequate counsel/parental presence)
intense media pressure creating public frenzy
